subject: Hosted API pricing — monthly token estimate & peak TPS confirmation
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, ethan.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: hosted API pricing inputs we discussed

Jordan — thanks again for the quick call today. Short recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can produce an apples-to-apples hosted estimate: 

Summary of what I heard from your team:
- Primary use: customer-facing assistant (search + summarization + light generation) across web and mobile.
- Expected first-year ramp: pilots in Q2, GA in Q4.
- Latency sensitivity: 95th %ile <= 400ms for chat flows.

Info we need to finalize a hosted pricing proposal (please confirm):
1) Expected monthly token volume (approx range ok) — examples: 10M / 50M / 200M tokens.
2) Peak TPS (tokens/s) during busy periods and sustained TPS target (e.g., 30s bursts vs sustained 5 TPS).
3) Target unit economics — is there a target $/1M tokens you need us to hit for budget approvals?
4) Any hard budget range for P0 (pilot) and P1 (GA).

Action items we’ll take once we have those numbers:
- Attach a lightweight cost model (MVP_pricing_model.xlsx) showing tiered pricing assumptions and impact of batching/quantization.
- Provide two scenarios: hosted standard SLO and low-latency premium (smaller batch windows).
- Draft SOW and procurement checklist for your finance team.

If it helps, Ben can do a short call with procurement to walk through payment terms and PO flow. Ethan will map the TPS numbers to instance sizing and warm pool behavior.

Thanks — if you can reply with the ranges later today/tomorrow that would be great.

— Mina
Mina Haddad

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Raman <asha.raman@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: hosted API pricing inputs we discussed

Thanks Mina — appreciate the tidy recap. Answers below (high level, will confirm with eng/procurement tomorrow):

1) Monthly token volume (estimate):
- Pilot (Q2): 20M–40M tokens/month.
- Ramp (Q3): 80M–150M tokens/month.
- GA (Q4+): planning for 200M–350M tokens/month depending on adoption.

2) Peak TPS:
- Typical peak (concurrent user surge): ~35–45 TPS observed during internal load tests.
- Sustained baseline TPS: ~6–8 TPS (steady daytime traffic).
- Spiky events: short bursts up to ~80 TPS for 2–3 minutes during product launches (we'd expect fallback behavior).

3) Target unit economics:
- For budget board approval we’re aiming for sub-$350 per 1M tokens on hosted. For GA scale, finance would like to see options down to ~$250/1M if we commit to volume.

4) Budget ranges:
- Pilot: $6k–$12k/month (OPEX).
- GA initial run: $40k–$120k/month depending on adoption.

We’ll float a formal procurement timeline tomorrow — Asha is looped for procurement/PO details.

—Jordan

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Quick sizing + unit-econ scenarios (attached model)

Jordan — thanks for the ranges. I attached a simple workbook (MVP_pricing_model.xlsx) but called out the key buckets here so you can see the levers: 

Assumptions used: avg tokens per request = 400 tokens (range 200–800), model = open-llama-70B-quant (example), warm pool target = 2x baseline concurrency.

Scenario A — Low-latency (smaller batches):
- 200M tokens/month → effective throughput need ≈ 77 TPS avg, peak 45–80 TPS
- Estimated hosted list price (no commit): ~$420 / 1M tokens
- With 12-month volume commitment & batching/quantization optimizations: ~$300 / 1M tokens

Scenario B — Cost-first (aggressive batching & heavier quant):
- 200M tokens/month → same token count but higher batching → lower instance counts
- Estimated: ~$240–270 / 1M tokens with a 12-month commit and warm pool tuning

Notes on peak TPS and warm pools:
- For short bursts (<= 3 minutes) we rely on burst capacity; sustained high TPS requires reserved capacity to keep cold-starts minimal.
- If you need 95th %ile latency <= 400ms we recommend a small warm pool and lower batch window which increases per-token cost ~10–20% vs cost-first scenario.

Next steps we suggest:
- Confirm token distribution (avg tokens per call) so we can iterate the workbook.
- If finance has a target like $250/1M for GA, we can model a 12–18 month commit + modest discount banding.

— Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ethan.park@redwood.ai

[Attachment: MVP_pricing_model.xlsx]
